author: kingpanther13
releaseNotes:
v4.3.11 - 2026-09-20
- chore: retire the Hub Security credential settings on firmware 2.5.0+ (#450)
  - Hub Security credentials are no longer needed, and the Hub Security section is no longer shown, on hub firmware 2.5.0 and later. An app's requests to the hub's internal API are exempt from the hub login, so these credentials never had any effect. Anything previously stored is cleared automatically the first time the app saves.
  - Hubs on firmware older than 2.5.0 keep the Hub Security section and its current behaviour.

v4.3.10 - 2026-09-19
- feat: rework hub_report_issue and record MCP client identity (#442)
  - `hub_report_issue` reports now show how the client connected (LAN or cloud relay), the MCP client's self-reported name, version and protocol version, the model in use, a snapshot of the app's settings and per-tool overrides, and dedicated sections for verbatim tool calls and client-side log lines. The tool tells the agent what is still missing, to enable debug logging and reproduce before filing, and to ask you (never guess) which app and model you use when the client cannot be identified, for example behind an mcp-remote bridge.
  - `hub_get_info` now includes the last MCP client seen (`mcpClient`), and the app logs each client's protocol version when it connects.

v4.3.9 - 2026-09-19
- fix: copy a variable into a String target through valStringOp (#445)
  - Copying one variable into another now works for text variables, not just numbers
  - Copying into a Boolean or DateTime variable is refused up front instead of leaving a half-built action

v4.3.8 - 2026-09-18
- feat: optional digit suffix on hub tool names (#444)
  - New Advanced setting "Tool name number" (off by default): adds a digit after "hub" in every tool name (e.g. `hub3_get_info`) so you can connect more than one hub's MCP server to the same AI client without tool-name collisions. Reconnect your client after changing it.

v4.3.7 - 2026-09-17
- fix: Rule Machine variable, settle, this-rule and wording corrections (#441)
  - Deleting a hub variable now checks whether the hub reports it in use (for example by a Rule Machine rule) and asks for confirmation first
  - Rules whose Required Expression is currently false are no longer reported as having an incomplete trigger after an update
  - Set Private Boolean actions can now target "this rule", on its own or together with other rules
  - Clearer rule health messages and a more accurate description of how Rule Machine evaluates mixed AND/OR expressions

v4.3.6 - 2026-09-16
- ci: publish fork PR library bundles after e2e approval (#436)
- ci: scan only the fork files the e2e job executes (#440)
- fix: report unverified standalone rule edits and recovery outcomes (#437)
  - Report rule edits whose health could not be verified after a timeout, with instructions to check the committed rule before proceeding.
  - Make automatic-recovery and rollback messages accurately describe whether recovery succeeded.

v4.3.5 - 2026-09-15
- fix: build Boolean variable conditions and keep walkStep drive state between steps (#426)
  - Rule Machine rules can now use Boolean hub variables in IF conditions and Required Expressions (for example "IF myBool is true")
  - Step-by-step rule building is more reliable, and a build that ends unfinished (such as an IF with no END-IF) is now reported as a failure

v4.3.4 - 2026-09-15
- fix: stop bulk rule edits at the first failed or partial item (#425)
  - Rule Machine bulk edits now stop at the first trigger or action that fails, instead of carrying on and turning the rule on half-built
    - Anything after the failure is reported as "not attempted", and the rule is left unfinalised so it can be repaired or restored from the automatic backup

v4.3.3 - 2026-09-14
- docs: recommend mcp-remote for Claude Desktop on all platforms (#430)
  - Claude Desktop setup now uses `mcp-remote` on Windows and macOS, replacing `mcp-proxy`.
    - If you use `uvx mcp-proxy`, switch to the new config in the README. Slow writes such as rule creation now complete in Claude Desktop instead of showing a generic error.
- fix: coordinate retained backups and recovery state (#419)
  - Keep rollback backups discoverable through concurrent updates and failed deletion, and enforce consistent backup retention.
  - Remove obsolete native-rule recovery records after confirmed app deletion while preserving active recovery intent.

v4.3.2 - 2026-09-14
- fix: complete sandbox Map validation and enforce blocking lint (#418)
  - Preserve device, rule, room, and dashboard data whose names overlap Hubitat's restricted Map-access names.
  - Keep backup and undo handles retrievable and preserve the original backup during repeated edits.
  - Report when a source restore has no verified undo backup, and avoid creating duplicate rules after a temporary configuration-read failure.
  - Use the current library version for rapid updates while retaining the original backup.

v4.3.1 - 2026-09-13
- fix: run MRTR writes in the first request instead of a mutation-free preflight (#422)
  - Slow-write tools (rules, native apps, drivers, virtual devices, device updates) now complete in a single request when they finish quickly. Clients that do not implement MCP request-to-request continuation no longer fail these writes with a generic error.
    - Long-running writes still continue automatically on clients that support it, and the server now tells models not to repeat a write after a bodyless client error without reading the target first.
    - Tool argument errors now come back as tool results rather than protocol errors, so assistants reliably see the reason and can correct the call themselves.

v4.3.0 - 2026-09-11
- fix: expire retained request state reliably (#417)
  - Remove expired continuation records without waiting for another write, and avoid repeatedly retrying failed metadata cleanup on every request.
- fix: use native device operations while honoring the allowlist (#420)
  - Device tools use native hub operations while continuing to honor device selection when allowlist bypass is disabled.
  - Configuration updates verify saved values and preserve hidden device metadata more precisely.
  - Virtual-device creation and device deletion provide clearer results when follow-up verification is incomplete.
  - Numeric attributes in poll results and list/context states retain native numeric values instead of always being strings.
  - Device health uses a bulk native activity read; missing metadata is reported as unknown.
  - The context resources and device-list filters read the whole inventory in one bulk hub request; one unreadable device is reported as metadata-unavailable instead of failing the list.
  - Attribute polling keeps its requested interval regardless of native read latency.
  - Health diagnostics use background continuations on supported clients to avoid blocking a cloud-relay response during network probes.
